scope: Dated national discovery snapshot and four selected local measures checked against official records. Not an exhaustive ballot database or a personalized sample ballot. No automatic election-results feed is connected.

snapshot.limit: Source publication date, not a live count. Local measures do not apply to every voter in the listed state. An unlisted state is not a verified zero. The national totals are separate from the four detailed examples.

measures.title: Question 1 · A new land use
measures.effect: Changes which uses voters authorize in this area
measures.summary: Decide whether data centers may be an authorized use in the Eldorado Valley Transfer Area, outside its habitat-conservation easement.
measures.yes: Allow data centers as a permitted use in the specified area. The council could consider future leases.
measures.no: Keep data centers outside the authorized uses in that area.
measures.limit: Approval would not require the council to approve a facility. This question does not govern land elsewhere in Boulder City. Campaign arguments in the official booklet are advocacy, not verified environmental measurements.
measures.question: What would each future lease require for water, electricity, noise, emissions and public infrastructure costs?

measures.title: Ordinance 2025-02 · A rezoning vote
measures.effect: Determines whether the rezoning takes effect
measures.summary: A referendum on changing specified land from agricultural-residential to general-industrial zoning for a proposed data-center development.
measures.outcome: Township record: the ordinance will not take effect following the August 4 election.
measures.limit: This concerns the specified rezoning, not a statewide prohibition. The dashboard does not report a certified vote tally.
measures.question: What zoning and permit decisions still apply to the site after this result?

measures.title: Measure NDC · A citywide prohibition
measures.summary: A General Plan amendment to prohibit data centers throughout Monterey Park, with the prohibition continuing until voters end it.
measures.yes: Adopt the proposed citywide prohibition through the General Plan amendment.
measures.no: Do not adopt this proposed General Plan amendment.
measures.outcome: City update identifies Measure NDC as adopted. No certified vote tally is reproduced here.
measures.limit: A no vote would not itself approve a project or remove other applicable restrictions. The ballot’s stated health and utility-rate purposes are not measured health outcomes.
measures.question: How is the city implementing the prohibition, and how does it define the facilities covered?

sources.label: City election page · measure and analysis

measures.title: Tax-increment districts · Who gets the next vote?
measures.effect: Adds a referendum requirement for qualifying districts
measures.summary: An ordinance requiring voter approval before the city creates or approves specified tax-increment districts involving large capital expenditures or the stated $10 million thresholds.
measures.yes: Require a referendum before approving a district covered by the ordinance.
measures.no: Do not add this referendum requirement through the proposed ordinance.
measures.outcome: Election-night county report: 2,710 yes and 1,371 no. This is the April 7 report, not a certified canvass verified by this dashboard.
measures.limit: This is a financing and approval-process measure, not a general data-center ban. Consult the full text for the distinct base-value and project-cost thresholds; it does not establish a campus’s tax payment.
measures.question: Which future financing districts are covered, and who bears repayment and infrastructure risks?
